articleTitle: Optical fiber in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer based on dual internal mirrors formed by a hollow sphere pair
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a fiber in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometer based on dual internal mirrors formed by a hollow sphere pair and fabricated by femtosecond laser micromachining together with fusion splicing technique. The hollow sphere surface adjacent to the fiber core can reflect part of the incident light beam to the air-cladding interface where, the light beam is reflected again before returning to the fiber core by another hollow sphere surface and recombining with the light beam remain in the fiber core. Such an interferometer is miniature and robust, and can effectively response to the environmental variations.

articleTitle: Optical characteristics of UV-LED with subwavelength grating
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Subwavelength grating structure with a thickness of 150nm was fabricated on ultraviolet light emitting diode by using electron beam lithography and inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching. For an optimal designed period, the subwavelength grating exhibit high polarization selectivity for the wavelength from 365nm to 400nm. Especially, a polarization ratio (TE/TM) of 3.5 was achieved for 365nm. Applying this characteristics, we demonstrated highly polarized UV-LED.

articleTitle: Low-loss silicon partial-rib waveguide polarization rotator
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A silicon partial-rib waveguide polarization rotator is designed, fabricated and characterized. The rotator, which consists of an asymmetric rib waveguide and a nano-taper waveguide, is suitable to simultaneous fabrication with a silicon optical modulator. The rotator has low excess loss of 0.5–1.5 dB and polarization extinction ratio higher than 10 dB in 1500–1600 nm.

articleTitle: Acceleration of wavelength switching for tunable distributed amplification (TDA-) DFB lasers
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The feedforward controller is designed and demonstrated to accelerate the wavelength switching for the tunable distributed amplification (TDA) DFB lasers. The controller has an impulse overshoot waveform so as to induce prompt transition of short time phenomena. The controlled laser shows a wavelength switching time of 150 ns which shows effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Polymer waveguide-type Kretschmann-structure surface plasmon sensor at 1550nm wavelength range
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Polymer waveguide-type Kretschmann-structure surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor was studied for compact, low-cost remote sensing application operated at 1550nm wavelength range. In order to confirm the fundamental operation, a concentration of 2-propanol in water was changed to attain 136/RIU.

articleTitle: Simulation of arrays of metal nanowires using a monochromatic recursive convolution finite-difference time-domain method
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We developed a monochromatic version of recursive convolution finite-difference time-domain method and used the same to compute the extinction spectra of arrays of silver nanowires. Results show that the localized surface plasmon resonance properties depend on the separation between two neighboring nanowires.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of low loss 1×8 silica-based phased array switch with low power consumption
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We achieved a low insertion loss of 3.6-6.8 dB and low power consumption of 1.6 W in 1 ×8 silica-based phased array switch by optimizing the number of arrayed waveguides.

articleTitle: Mach-Zehnder filter using multiple Si waveguide structure sections with polarization independence or splitter function attained by custom-made interference conditions
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We report the Mach-Zehnder interferometer wavelength filter using multiple Si wire waveguide structure sections. The property of the phase shift or interference conditions can be designed to attain many types of functionality. The polarization insensitive device was obtained in the experiment. The polarization beam splitting can also be achieved by dedicated design procedure.

articleTitle: Optical amplifier assisted cavity ring down spectroscopy (CRDS) method for compact infrared sensing
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Waveguide based CRDS is attractive for its possibility of realizing compact breath sensing system. The waveguide propagation loss, however, loses the light power that leads to the degradation of the sensitivity. We propose optical amplifier assisted CRDS method to detect 0.5% CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> for the case of utilizing such loss waveguide.

articleTitle: Temperature stabilization of high-power led chips using low-cost passive heat sinks
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We present a numerical analysis and experimental measurements of the temperature stabilization of high-power LED chips that we have obtained by employing an aluminium passive heat sink, designed to be used in a compact light bulb configuration. We demonstrate that our system keeps the temperature of the LED chip well-below 60°C yielding long-term operation of the device. Our simulations have been performed for a device of low fabrication costs and which enables an easy installation in public streetlights. The experimental measurements performed in different configurations show a nice agreement with the numerical calculations.

articleTitle: Facile preparations of au nanostructures for SERS
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Nanoscale Au materials are very promising optical materials for a wide range of applications. Development of facile preparation methods of new nanostructured Au materials with good optical properties is an urgent theme. We have developed simple new methods for nanoscale Au materials. 2-Thiophene derivatives can behave both as a reducing agent for Au precursor and surface capping ligands to guide the nanostructures of Au.

articleTitle: Electro-optic polymer waveguides fabrication using thermal imprint lithography technology
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Electro-optic (EO) polymer is a promising candidate for active materials in realizing optical modulator. It offers high-speed switching and high-bandwidth optical modulator devices. We study thermally-curable polycyanurate (PCN) doped high nonlinear optical chromophore (DPT) to create a guest-host EO polymer with thermally stable second-order nonlinearity. We fabricated the PCN-based EO optical waveguide by using simple thermal imprint lithography technology using silicone mold and we realized a single-mode propagation at a wavelength of 1300 nm by fine-tuning the refractive index of the core and cladding materials.

articleTitle: Laser application on plant factory
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Essential resource elements in crop production are light, water, carbon dioxide and fertilizer. Optimum design for air-conditioning and lightings in plant factory system is required to realize the economical operation of plant factory because most energy consuming elements of plant factory system are air-conditioning and lightings. In this sense application of solid state lighting sources such as LED in plant factory system have been promoted to expect some reduction of running cost in lighting. Research work of solid state laser application in plant factory has just started recently at Osaka Prefecture University Plant Factory Research Center. The latest development of laser application research in plant factory will be reported in this article.

articleTitle: Novel 3D die-stacked opto-electronic transceiver ICs that allow for waferscale fabrication
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Optical interconnects can offer small footprint, high bandwidth density and high data rates. In this paper we demonstrate a wafer scale fabrication process of the 3D stacked transceivers which leads to very high bandwidth density as well as potential low cost. Uniform open eye patterns at 10 Gb/s/channel of both 3D stacked transmitter and receiver ICs indicates that the interconnection technology suggested is robust.

articleTitle: Solution processed organic light-emitting diodes and photodiodes utilizing poly (alkylfluorene) derivatives
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Organic materials have advantages for simple fabrication by solution process such as printing technique. Solution processed organic devices have been studied using poly(alkyljluorene) derivatives. This study focused on fabrication of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) including solution processed electrode and the increased photo sensitivity of solution-processed organic photodiodes (OPDs). Solution processed OLEDs with Ag nano-ink as cathode electrode have been successfully fabricated and highly efficient blue-light sensitive photodiodes have been successfully fabricated using poly(alkyljluorene) derivative and soluble hole transport materials.

articleTitle: Preparation of highly luminescent CdSe quantum dots by reverse micelles
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Highly luminescent CdSe quantum dots (QDs) were prepared by AOT microemulsion method. The optimal reaction time for CdSe synthesis was 2h and the highest PL efficiency was obtained when W was 5 and the ratio of Cd/Se was 2. Under these conditions, the PL efficiency of 30% could be obtained.

articleTitle: Conversion of two polarizations into different order single polarization modes using slanted sidewall silicon wire waveguide and its application to polarization independent wavelength filtering
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A waveguide with slanted sidewall is used to convert the fundamental TM mode to 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order TE mode. The fundamental TE mode is unchanged. The two polarizations are converted to different order modes with the same polarization. Polarization independent wavelength filtering can be attained using this mode converter with AWG or devices which operates only for the TE mode.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of holographic data storage system with phase-shift embedded SQAM datapages
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We quantitatively investigate the performance of holographic data storage system with Spatial Quadrature Amplitude Modulation datapages in which intensity and phase modulations are combined. The phase-shift required for phase demodulation is embedded in the datapage. Root Mean Square Error of demodulated phase value and Symbol Error Rate are experimentally evaluated.

articleTitle: Wavelength selective switch with high angular dispersion element based on Bragg reflector waveguide
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a prototype wavelength selective switch (WSS), composed of a Bragg reflector waveguide dispersion element. Thanks to large angular-dispersion and dense-array integration of the Bragg reflector waveguide, the prototype WSS with 6-port operation can be scaled up for supporting over 100 ports operation, maintaining its compact size.

articleTitle: Effect of light incidence angle on optical absorption characteristics of bulk heterojunction organic solar cells
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We have computationally analysed how the light incident angle influences the absorption characteristics of bulk heterojunction solar cells by the electro-magnetic field analysis method. The absorbed optical power in three different active layers was calculated by using the Poynting's theorem, resulting that it was significantly decreased under the incidence angle larger than 30° by the optical interference. In addition, we understood that the absorptivity of lower band-gap active layers could be more affected by the incidence angle variation.

articleTitle: Characterization and analysis of the roughness induced double-dip spectrum of SOI micro-ring resonator
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Backscattering due to roughness is evident from the presence of a double-dip in micro-ring filter spectrum. We present both experimental and theoretical studies, based on a generalized ring model including the backscattering effect to provide an accurate analysis of the ring properties that shed light on the surface roughness due to fabrication.

articleTitle: Probing substrate influence on graphene by fitting Raman signals with Voigt profile
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We provide a new approach to identify the substrate influence and doping effect on graphene surface. In this work, the Raman bandwidths of G bands were fitted into the Voigt profile. The bandwidths of Lorentzian parts were kept as constant whether it is the suspended and supported graphene. For the Gaussian part, the suspended graphene exhibit a much greater Gaussian bandwidths of than supported graphene. It reveals the doping effect on supported graphene is stronger than that of suspended graphene. We also analyze the peak-positions of G bands, and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2D</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> ratios. For the suspended graphene, the peak positions of G band are downshifted respect to supported graphene, and the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2D</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> ratios of suspended graphene are larger than those of supported graphene.

articleTitle: High-speed hybrid integrated, 1×2 wavelength selective switch using PLZT optical switches and silica planar lightwave circuits
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A hybrid integration of silica arrayed-waveguide gratings, couplers and a high-speed PLZT switch array is reported for the first time. A 1×2 wavelength selective switch is fabricated. The channel spacing is 200 GHz and the number of channels is 20. The switching time is less than 13 ns.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation in all solid photonic crystal fiber with flat all-normal dispersion
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Experimental demonstration of supercontinuum in an in-house fabricated, all-solid, flat-top normal dispersion photonic crystal fiber is given. Presented study comprises characterization of developed fiber in terms of microstructure design, attenuation and dispersion characteristic, followed by experiment and numerical analysis of supercontinuum generation spanning an octave from around 900 nm to 2400 nm under 1530 nm excitation with 70 fs pulses.

articleTitle: Coherence changes in partially coherent beams transmitted by metal gratings
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We study the coherence changes in beams transmitted by binary metallic gratings that support surface plasmons. It is shown that by choosing suitable parameters for the grating, the degree of coherence of the beam can be significantly increased.

articleTitle: Design, fabrication, and characterization of hybrid structure
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: In this study a mold of a line generator consisting of a cylindrical lens array with a triangular diffractive pattern was ultra-precision diamond machined and replicated to UV curable polymer. The structure was then characterized and tested, and proven to function as designed.

articleTitle: Coherent random laser fluid of nematic liquid crystal emulsions
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Reported here is a coherent (resonant) random laser fluid of nematic liquid crystal (LC) emulsion in water. It is a low viscosity fluid like a usual liquid. The optical loop forms among the LC droplets and its length is evaluated to be approximately 150 micrometers. The LC emulsion is useful for the investigation of the mechanism of the random laser because it is a fluid and easy to change the scatterer density.

articleTitle: All optical flip-flop and inverter using adjacent lasing wavelengths emitting from semiconductor microring laser
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrated all optical flip-flop and inverter using two adjacent lasing wavelengths by a semiconductor MQW microring laser. The lasing wavelength (1567.54nm) and both side adjacent lasing wavelengths (1565.84nm and 1569.24nm) were used as the injection light wavelength. These operations were realized in the same device with different control current.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Mgo:LiNbO3 thin film ridge waveguide by surface-activated bonding and ion slicing
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We report the fabrication of MgO:LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> waveguides by surface-activated bonding with Au layers and ion slicing. He<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ions were used for implantation. The films of 1 μm thickness were obtained on SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/Au layers. The ridge waveguides are also demonstrated. We achieved strong optical confinement at 1550 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: Dielectric function dependence on temperature for noble metal
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: In this paper, we provide an empirical function to describe the temperature dependence of dielectric function for Au. The empirical function shows a good agreement with previous results and handbook. Through the empirical function, one can obtain the dielectric constant of Au at arbitrary temperature and wavelength. This database is useful for the applications that the SP resonance at high temperature, such as the plasmonic thermal emitter, SP-assisted thermal cancer treatment and so on.

articleTitle: Construction of metal-enhanced evanescent-wave microcavity and air-gap control
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A metallic air-gap planar microcavity based on enhanced evanescent waves was constructed from a dielectric/metal/air gap/metal. Modulation of the interference of light through the air gap was performed using a small mechanical variation of the air-gap distance. The demonstration shows that the air-gap distance is controlled in submicron scale.

articleTitle: Nano-imprint method for metal-assisted guided mode resonance biosensor
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A high sensitivity metal-assisted guided mode resonance biosensor is fabricated by nano-imprint method. All the MaGMR chips are designed resonating in fundamental TE mode. The resonance wavelength can be tuned from 800nm to 870nm with bulk sensitivity varied from 200nm/RIU to 600nm/RIU. The measurement data shows good agreements with simulations.

articleTitle: Electro-optic polarization conversion type modulator for short-wavelength light using periodically poled MgO:LiNbO3
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrated electro-optic polarization conversion type modulator for violet light using periodically poled MgO doped LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> for the first time. High-quality periodically poled structures with 3.6 μm period were obtained over 1.0 × 1.0 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area. The modulation of violet light was accomplished, and the conversion efficiency of 78% was obtained.

articleTitle: OCT-based measurement of Rayleigh-wave velocity in soft Materials
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a new technique for measuring the propagation velocity of Rayleigh wave, or surface acoustic wave (SAW), using swept-source optical coherence tomography (OCT). We establish a theory for calculating the SAW velocity of tissues based on the measured OCT images, which is then experimentally verified using agar and tissue samples. The SAW velocity calculated by this technique agrees well with the previous results.

articleTitle: Tb/s optical communications using orbital angular momentum
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: In this paper, we discuss recent advancements in the use of orbital angular momentum for increasing channel capacity and spectral efficiency by spatially multiplexing multiple data channels. We also describe Tbit/s transmission results as well as basic demonstrations of switching and networking functions.

articleTitle: Hot embossing technology for development of glass microoptics with broadband transmission in visible and mid infrared ranges
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We describe the application of the hot embossing process to fabricate micro-optical elements using multi-component soft glasses. The fabricated elements are both refractive and diffractive and can be used in the visible to mid-infrared range. We will present all steps of the fabrication process and optical properties of obtained elements.

articleTitle: Sensing distance elongation in BOTDR scheme using optical frequency comb
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We propose distance elongation of BOTDR fiber sensors using optical frequency comb (OFC) as a lightsourse. As the OFC increased fiber transmitted power compared to single frequency light, it is expected to elongate the distance.

articleTitle: Proposal of optical mode switch configuration for four modes
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We propose optical mode switch configuration for four modes for the first time. It switches one mode to another among 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> to 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> modes, while keeping compact size of 0.033mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including input/output access waveguides. Less than -19dB mode-crosstalk is expected in the present configuration.

articleTitle: Tolerance to phase and amplitude deviations in optical waveguide circuit for recognition of 16QAM codes
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Optical processing of optical labels is expected in photonic label routers. We propose optical circuits to recognize optical QAM codes. The circuits are multi-stage connection of previously proposed circuit for QPSK code recognition. The recognition characteristics for 16QAM codes and their tolerance to phase and amplitude deviations are theoretically analyzed.

articleTitle: Spatial mode multiplexer/demultiplexer based on tapered hollow waveguide with lateral optical confinement structure
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a spatial-mode multiplexer/demultiplexer based on a tapered hollow waveguide with lateral optical confinement. The fabricated device shows vertical radiation spots for different spatial transverse-modes traveling along a tapered hollow waveguide. Both multiplexing and demultiplexing functions are presented, exhibiting a potential of 2D spatial-mode multiplexing/demultiplexing devices in compact fashion.

articleTitle: A wavelength-selective switch based on microring resonators and Mach-Zehnder interferometer switches
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A wavelength-selective switch composed of microring resonators (MRRs) and Mach-Zehnder interferometer thermo-optic switches is demonstrated with an output on/off ratio of 9.7 dB for a selected wavelength channel. The degradation of the transmittance of WSS is addressed due to the difference in resonant wavelength between MRRs coupled to input and output bus lines.

articleTitle: Silicon photonic advanced modulation format transceivers
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Silicon photonic circuits guide light inside silicon waveguides on a silicon substrate. Proponents of silicon photonics usually focus on high-volume, low-cost applications, such as short-reach interconnects, because of silicon's large-scale manufacturability. However, silicon photonics is even better suited for high-end telecommunications applications such as advanced modulation formats, because of its high index contrast and high element yield. This talk focuses on advanced modulation format transceivers using silicon photonics.

articleTitle: Direct optical coupling to a SMF array with a multi-channel lens-integrated surface-emitting DFB laser for a low-cost optical module
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Direct optical coupling between a four-channel lens-integrated surface-emitting DFB array and a SMF array was demonstrated. A very narrow emission beam was produced by monolithic lens integration, and all four channels were thus simultaneously coupled to a SMF array with large tolerance of +/- 5.5μ m at excess loss of -1 dB.

articleTitle: First demonstration of liquid concentration measurement by using silica high-mesa waveguide
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the concentration measurement of liquid by using silica high-mesa waveguide for the first time. It proves that a certain portion of the propagation light has profiled out actually from the waveguide. Moreover, the concentration measurement of 2% ethanol was also confirmed successfully.

articleTitle: Integrated silicon grating waveguides with ferroelectric liquid crystal cladding for optical tunable wavelength filters
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A tunable wavelength filter array with sampled grating Si-waveguides and ferroelectric liquid crystal cladding is proposed and fabricated. Bistable tuning operation with about 0.8-nm shift in wavelength characteristics was demonstrated.

articleTitle: High extinction-ratio characteristics over 60 db Mach-Zehnder modulator with asymmetric power splitting y-branches on x-cut Ti:LiNbO3
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We investigated a Mach-Zehnder modulator with asymmetric power splitting Y-branches. Output characteristics of a modulator depend on the relation between the power splitting ratios of the front and back Y-branches. By tuning the power splitting ratio of the front Y-branch, we achieved maximum power output operation and high extinction-ratio operation respectively.

articleTitle: 10-Gbit/s on-chip optical interconnect module using silicon-based 45° micro-reflectors terminated polymer waveguides
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: In this paper, we propose a 10-Gbit/s optical interconnect module realized on the silicon optical bench (SiOB) using the silicon-based 45° micro-reflectors terminated the polymer waveguides. The silicon-based 45° micro-reflectors are fabricated on an orientation-defined (100) silicon substrate by using anisotropic chemical wet etching. The VCSEL and PD chips are assembled at the input and output ports of proposed module to demonstrate an out-of-plane optical coupling for the on-chip optical interconnects. The transmission efficiency of as high as -2.8 dB is experimentally obtained with a polymer-waveguide length of 0.5 cm. The clearly 10-Gbit/s electrical eye pattern is obtained and verifies that such a proposed module is suitable for the optical interconnects.

articleTitle: SOI-based vertically-splitting optical waveguides for optical interconnects
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A SOI-based three-dimensional vertically-splitting optical waveguides for optical interconnects is experimentally demonstrated first time. The optical insertion loss of -3.46 dB is experimentally obtained for the proposed splitter with tuneable splitting ratio from 4.9:1 to 1.2:1. Compared with the straight waveguide, the proposed waveguide have excess loss of 0.51 dB.

articleTitle: Low driving power push-pull modulator for multi-wavelength modulation and 4×4 switch using silicon microring resonator loaded Mach-Zehnder interferometers by thermo-optic effect
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the low-driving power/voltage characteristics of a cascaded push-pull microring Mach-Zehnder modulator (MRR MZM) for multiple-wavelength modulation and a 4 ×4 switch using silicon microring loaded MZ interferometers driven by thermo-optic effect. The driving voltage is reduced up-to 1/3 in the MZM and power up-to 1/2 in the switch.

articleTitle: Noise tolerance in QPSK label recognition with optical passive waveguide circuits
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: In photonic label routing networks, recognition of optical labels is one of the key functions. We have proposed waveguide-type optical circuits for recognition of optical labels encoded in quadri-phase-shift-keying (QPSK) form. We discuss contrast ratio in the label recognition outputs and its degradation due to additive noise was discussed.

articleTitle: First demonstration of high intrinsic modulation bandwidth (26.4 GHz) in active multimode interferometer laser diode by using split pumping configuration
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: High intrinsic 3dB modulation bandwidth in asymmetric active multimode interferometer laser diode is demonstrated by using split pumping configuration. Significant enhancement of 3 dB intrinsic bandwidth up to 24.6 GHz has been confirmed successfully by using this scheme.

articleTitle: Infrared thermometry for detecting flaws in large-core polymer optical fibers
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We develop a cost-effective method for detecting flaws in large-core polymer optical fibers based on infrared thermometry. When the propagating light is 282 mW at 1.55 μm the temperature dependence of the optical loss at the flaw is linear with a proportionality constant of 0.74 dB/°C which can be enhanced using high-power light source.

articleTitle: VCSEL — Its conception, development, and future
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) is becoming a key device in high-speed optical local-area networks (LAN) and even wide-area networks (WAN). This device is also enabling ultra parallel data transfer in equipment and computer systems including storage area networks (SAN) and wide optoelectronics fields. In this paper, we will review its conception, physics, and the progress of technology covering the spectral band from infrared to ultraviolet by featuring materials and fabrication technology. Performances such as threshold, output power, polarization, modulation, and reliability are introduced. Lastly, we will touch on its future prospects.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional integrated optical interconnect with laser and photodetector on SOI substrate
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A three-dimensional on-chip optical interconnect with laser and photodetector is demonstrated using guided-wave silicon optical bench with 45-degree micro-reflector. Three-dimensional optical path is employed to connect laser and photodetector. The optical coupling efficiency between laser and photodetector is -1.74dB. 5-Gbps error-free data transmission with 6mA laser bias is measured.

articleTitle: Hybrid digital holography that combines simultaneous and temporal phase-shifting interferometric techniques
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A hybrid digital holography technique that combines simultaneous phase-shifting interferometric technique characterized by high temporal resolution and temporal phase-shifting interferometric technique characterized by high spatial resolution is proposed. Effectiveness of the technique is confirmed by recording the digital holograms of moving objects with various migration speeds and performing computational reconstruction.

articleTitle: Optical waveguide resonator for one-port refractive index sensing
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We report an optical waveguide sensor using ring resonator. A refractive index sensor using resonator with vertical light input will be described. A grating coupler is used to couple the light beam to waveguide and output the light beam. The device has diameter of 40 μm with 500 nm wide waveguide, and fabricated in silicon on insulator (SOI). Experiments show that it has 313 nm/RIU sensitivity and detection limit of 1.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> RIU for changes in the refractive index of the sample.

articleTitle: Rigorous surface-plasmon polaritons at a lossy interface
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Making use of a rigorous treatment, we demonstrate that the approximate results that are customarily employed for the analysis of a plasmon field at a metal/dielectric boundary are incorrect even in some situations in which they are supposed to hold. We show further that the exact treatment implies the existence of a new type of backward-propagating polariton, analogous to the fields met in negative-index manmade structures. Such polariton is never encountered in the standard approximate analysis.

articleTitle: Optical focus with high aperture lens based on high contrast gratings
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Beam shaping of light on a micron scale is of particular importance when targeting integrated photonic applications. Here, we present a high numerical aperture lens based on high contrast gratings incorporating multiple phase shifts. We show successful fabrication and micron scale focusing which is beneficial to the micro-optics community.

articleTitle: Wavelength tuning and controlled temperature dependence of MEMS VCSELs with thermally and electrostatically actuated micromachined mirror
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the wavelength tuning of 850nm-GaAs-VCSELs with a controlled temperature dependence of wavelengths using a thermally and electrostatically actuated MEMS structure. The wavelength tuning and the control of the temperature dependence are independently realized. The result indicates a possibility of realizing tunable and athermal VCSELs with engineerd temperature dependence.

articleTitle: Micro-optics for intelligent displays
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Microoptics have become the key technology in liquid crystal display systems due to its capabilities of miniaturization and design flexibility. We presented active microoptical components for enhancing the image quality, providing better functions, increasing light efficiency, and generating 3D images in LCD applications.

articleTitle: Proposal of multiple slot silica high-mesa waveguide for infrared absorption
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We propose multiple slot silica high-mesa waveguide for infrared absorption, due to its possibility of realizing high portion of optical field out of the waveguide. It shows high portion of optical field out of the waveguide of 20.3%for fourfold structure at the wavelength of 1550nm.

articleTitle: Wavelength stabilization of tunable lasers based on thermal-drift canceler
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The wavelength stabilization based on the digitally controlled thermal-drift canceler is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The tunable distributed amplification (TDA-) DFB laser controlled by this canceler reaches the targeted wavelength within a microsecond and keeps it stably.

articleTitle: Array masters for UV-replication used in imaging applications
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: As demonstrated in microelectronics, the batch fabrication based on the processing of wafers can lead to a significant reduction in prize as well as in size. This concept was adapted to the fabrication of imaging optics extensively used in mobile phone cameras relying on small pixels but was limited in resolution. UV-replication is the standard technique for the objective fabrication where a liquid polymer, which fills the molding tool of the lenses, is hardened using UV-radiation. This technique is essential in single aperture objectives as well as in innovate array camera approaches which are at the stage of commercialization.

articleTitle: Flip-chip InGaN light-emitting diodes with an integrated microlens array
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The fabrication of hexagonally close-packed lens array on flip-chip bonded InGaN LED by nanosphere lithography is reported. A self-assembled monolayer of silica spheres with diameters of 1-μm serves as an etch mask to be transferred onto the sapphire face of the LED to form hemispherical lenses. Without degrading electrical characteristic, the light output power of lensed LED is increased by more than one-quart, compared with an unpatterned LED. The optical behavior of individual lenses and converging effect of lensed LED are by ray-tracing and confocal imaging.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics in free-space laser communications with error correction
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Free-space laser communications (FSO) is influenced by scintillation and propagation loss increases as the propagation distance becomes longer. Therefore, the communication quality is degraded. In this paper, we examined the propagation characteristics when error correction which is used to improve the communication quality in wireless communication is brought in FSO. As a result, it was confirmed that the communication quality was improved.

articleTitle: A highly polarized laser backlight for liquid crystal displays
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We designed and fabricated a new polarized laser backlight containing a light guide plate of a zero-zero-birefringence polymer. The degree of polarization of the output light around the normal direction was higher than 95 %. Moreover, the highly collimated output light was achieved resulting in high power efficiency.

articleTitle: Polymeric wavelength division multiplexing coupler with fiber guide and filter trench fabricated by one-step replication process for bi-directional communication
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A polymeric bi-directional wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) coupler for graded-index (GI) plastic optical fiber (PDF) was fabricated and characterized. The device with fiber guides and a filter trench was fabricated by simple one-step soft-lithography process. The insertion loss, the isolation and the directivity of the device at wavelengths of 850 nm and 790 nm was less than 3 dB, more than 20 dB and more than 20 dB respectively by optimally designing the structure. By setting GI-POFs in fiber guides and inserting a WDM filter in a filter trench with passive alignment, bi-directional communication was realized with more than 2.5 Gbps/λ for 150m length.

articleTitle: HCG reflectivity characteristics for a small-sized beam spot
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A high contrast grating (HCG) mirror was investigated in the case of the wavelength-scale small beam spot system by the numerical simulations. It was found that a reflectivity dependence on the spacer thickness showed a large reflectivity oscillation unlike a plane wave system. A thin spacer thickness was indispensable for a high reflectivity by suppression of the beam diffraction. The number of the HCG grating was also discussed and the number of covering the waveguide core area or more was important for high reflectivity. A 70% of reflectivity can be obtained by a single grating.

articleTitle: Photo-luminescence of rare earth complexes in the molecular films
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Two molecular films with wet-processes, modified stretched polymer film and modified Langmuir-Blodgett technique, were develop to obtain polarized ff emission. The polymer stretching ratios of former film have much effect on the polarized angles of polarized ff emission. The latter film can be control various combinations of compositions.

articleTitle: Development of efficient solar-pumped laser for renewable energy creation
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We developed Nd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>, Cr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-codoped laser crystals for solar-pumped lasers. We succeeded markedly in increasing the absorption in the UV-VIS region using Nd, Cr:YVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> and Nd, Cr:CaYAlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystals. The absorption cross section of the Nd, Cr:CaYAlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystal approximately 400 nm was more than 70 times that of Nd, Cr:YAG crystals.

articleTitle: Proposal and design of hybrid light guide plate for large-area LED display to improve illuminance and color uniformity
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A novel hybrid light guide plate (HLGP) for large area LED display was proposed and investigated the optical characteristics to improve the efficiency and properties by combining both advantages of the direct-type and edge-type backlights. Ray-tracing simulation shows that the illuminance uniformity and color coordinate deviation for the 55-inch HLGP are more than 84% and less than ±0.005, respectively. In addition, it has an advantage of thinner thickness and less number of LEDs compared to those of the commercial direct-type LED backlight.

articleTitle: Nonpolar GaN two dimensional photonic crystal H2 high quality factor nanocavities
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Nonpolar GaN two-dimensional photonic crystal (PC) H2 nanocavities have been realized and investigated. One dominated resonant mode was demonstrated at 388 nm with quality factor of approximately 4300 at 77K. Moreover, the degree of polarization of the emission from the non-polar GaN PC nanocavity was measured to be 64% along the m crystalline direction.

articleTitle: Liquid crystal microlens operated with fluorescent dyes
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Liquid crystal (LC) microlens could be a new type of micro optical components driven by an optical field. In this study, formation behavior of LC microlens was explored by doping several fluorescent dyes to reduce photo-thermal effect. Among the dyes, coumarin derivative-doped LC system showed lens effect with polarization selectivity.

articleTitle: Beam propagation in all-glass nanostructured gradient index microlenses
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the feasibility of using the nanostructured micro-optics technology to create a large diameter quantized elliptical microlens. Nanostructured gradient index elements have discrete internal structure with feature sizes much smaller than the wavelength of the incident light. Standard methods of GRIN microlens fabrication suffer from limited gadient value as well as from limited accuracy of gradient control. The nanostructured micro-optics fabrication technology, which exploits the techniques used in the fabrication of photonic crystal fibre, can be used to create a wide range of nanostructured gradient index micro-optical components. In this paper we demonstrate the feasibility of using the nanostructured micro-optics technology to create a 20-100 μm diameter quantized elliptical and spherical microlens.

articleTitle: Highly efficient OLED lighting for Eco-Solution
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Build-up light extraction substrates and high performance all-phosphorescent white OLEDs were investigated. The light extraction substrate was composed with high refractive index layer and texture on a glass substrate. As a result, high efficacy of 114 lm/W and long half-decay lifetime of 100,000 h at 1,000 cd/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> device with the emissive area of 1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was achieved. We also achieved high performance OLED device with the emissive area of 25cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, whose performance was equivalent with a 1cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-sized device.

articleTitle: Colorless optical add/drop using small matrix switch and cyclic AWG
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We describe a new wavelength routing switch architecture that uses small matrix switches and cyclic arrayed-waveguide gratings. This switch enables us to provide colorless add/drop ports in reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer nodes.

articleTitle: Design of efficient surface plasmon polariton modulator using graphene
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We numerically investigate graphene based surface plasmon polariton (SPP) waveguide modulators. We demonstrate that SPP waveguides with metal-air-metal structure can have a two times improvement in the figure of merit, defined by the ratio of extinction ratio to the voltage-off propagation loss, compared to indium-tin oxide based SPP electroabsorption modulators.

articleTitle: Aberration multiplexing in microholographic recording
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The feasibility of aberration multiplexing in microholographic recording was investigated through a numerical simulation. The multiplexing is performed by forming multiple microholograms at the same position by changing the aberration of recording beams and selectively reproducing each of multiple microholograms by changing the aberration of a readout beam. The simulation showed that multiplexing of more than 10 bits would be possible by combining the spherical, coma, and astigmatic aberrations.

articleTitle: Statistical properties of the electromagnetic field at blackbody cavity opening and in its far zone
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We consider radiation from a blackbody cavity opening and derive an explicit expression for the electric coherence matrix in the aperture and in its far zone. The aperture and far-zone coherence and polarization properties are assessed by measures valid for three-component fields. We analyse the far-zone coherence created by an incoherent, partially polarized planar source and show that paraxially it coincides with the blackbody result. Our conclusions are useful in modelling thermal sources and natural light.

articleTitle: Compact 5 × 5 wavelength-selective cross connect using integrated 2-D MEMS mirror arrays
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a 5 × 5 wavelength selective cross-connect (WSXC) constituted by two newly developed MEMS devices with 5 × 46 micro-mirrors arranged two-dimensionally and Monk-Gillieson spectroscopic optics system, which is applicable to a 100-GHz channel grid. The introduction of the optics system leads to a WSXC with a small volume of 180 × 170 × 40 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Micro-Alvarez lenses for a variable dynamic range Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The well-known Alvarez lenses consist of a pair of aspheric surfaces such that their relative lateral displacement results in an equivalent quadratic phase inducing lens that can be tuned from positive to negative powers by controlling the amount and direction of the displacements. In applications requiring a range of only positive powers, the use of the Alvarez lenses in their original design results in an inefficient use of plate size and equivalent lens aperture. We show formulas to shape the surfaces overcoming this inefficient problem. The design parameters to construct an array of micro-Alvarez lenses to compose a Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor with variable dynamic range is given.

articleTitle: Thermal control of diffraction wavelength in holographic polymer dispersed liquid crystal by using different grating structure
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A microperiodic structure composed of polymer and liquid crystal phases, called holographic polymer dispersed liquid crystal (HPDLC), is fabricated based on a photo-induced phase separation technique by laser interferometric exposure. The diffraction wavelength of HPDLC formed by different grating structures is experimentally investigated by spectroscopic measurements as a function of temperature at around 35°C. The HPDLC volume gratings composed of different film thickness show the controllability of diffraction wavelength between visible and infrared lights with a rise in temperature.

articleTitle: Angle-multiplexing recording of multi-context for optically reconfigurable gate array in holographic memory using liquid crystal composites
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A holographic polymer-dispersed liquid crystal (HPDLC) memory to record multi-context information for an optically reconfigurable gate array is formed by the angle-multiplexing recording using successive laser exposures in liquid crystal (LC) composites. The laser illumination system is constructed using the half mirror and photomask written by the different configuration contexts placed on the motorized stages under the control of a personal computer. The configuration contexts corresponding to the various logical circuits are reconstructed by the laser illumination at different incident angle in the HPDLC memory.

articleTitle: Structural dependence of the switching characteristics of 2×2 InAlGaAs/InAlAs Mach-Zehnder-type optical switch
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We fabricated 2×2 InAlGaAs/InAlAs Mach-Zehnder-type optical switches (MZ-OS) by employing the sophisticated fabrication process to control the structural parameters as much as possible. Low crosstalk and polarization-independent operation was confirmed, and at the same time it was also noticed that the switching characteristics are dependent on the structural parameters. Their tolerances are discussed.

articleTitle: Turnkey, high power dissipative soliton all fiber laser using a hybrid modelocking mechanism
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a turnkey, high power mode-locked all fiber laser modelocked by the hybrid modelocking mechanism consisting of a nonlinear amplifying loop mirror and a carbon nanotube-saturable absorber. Nitrogen sealing prevents damage of the nanotubes permitting long term stability at high output powers.

articleTitle: Multiple excitation of localized surface plasmon using metallic nano-particle array based sharp ridge nanoaperture
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a multiple excitation model of sharp ridge nanoaperture to create a small optical spot size with an extremely strong intensity. To verify the multiple excitation condition of the nanoaperture, the simulation is calculated by using three different metallic nanoparticle arrays, aluminium, silver, and gold. The intensity using aluminium and silver nanoparticle array is ~1.7and ~2.3 times higher than that of original nanoaperture. Furthermore, by shifting the location of NP array, the intensity is ~1.2 times and ~1.5 times higher than un-shifted one.

articleTitle: Noninvasive observation of vascular leakage induced by focused ultrasound with optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) is a recently discovered noninvasive technique for local and temporal enhancement of vascular permeability, which facilitates drug delivery from the vessels into the surrounding tissue. However, exposure to FUS at a high intensity may cause permanent damage. In this study, to investigate the effects of the FUS treatment on blood vessels, we proposed to use optical coherence tomography (OCT) for real-time observation. OCT can be implemented for the reconstruction of tissue microstructures. To quantitatively evaluate the morphological changes of the vessels after the FUS exposure with OCT, a new algorithm was proposed to estimate the vessel area, based on the comparison of backscattering properties resulting from the tissue and vascular structures. Results showed that the vessel area increased as the exposed power increased, and the area became significantly larger at a higher FUS exposure power of 10W. In conclusion, OCT observation can be potentially effective for monitoring the outcome and investigating effects of FUS treatment.

articleTitle: Capability of intensity-correlation spectral-domain optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We describe spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (OCT) based on classical intensity correlations. The setup employs a Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer as a classical analogue of quantum OCT. It is shown theoretically that it enables scanless cross-sectional imaging with dispersion cancellation and axial resolution enhancement. Some basic features of the technique are addressed.

articleTitle: Novel ballpoint pen interconnection for high speed graded index plastic optical fiber network
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We developed a cost effective and precise ballpoint pen termination designed for graded index polymer optical fiber, which realized high coupling efficiency despite rough connection. We invented a thin, lightweight, and flexible 120 Gb/s optical cable with compact interface, and demonstrated 8K ultra high definition video data transmission.

articleTitle: Timing detector using cross gain modulation in semiconductor optical amplifier for adaptive all-optical signal processing
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We propose a novel timing adjuster using a semiconductor optical amplifier to realize all-optical signal processing. We experimentally demonstrate error free operations for 10.7 Gbps return-to-zero on-off keyed signal input both in timing matched and mismatched conditions.

articleTitle: Characterization of fractional photothermolysis and visualization of microthermal zone with optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Summary form only given. In this study, an optical coherence tomography (OCT) system is implemented for the noninvasive characterization of photothermolysis in human skin induced by ablative fractional lasers (AFLs) and non-ablative fractional lasers (NAFLs). With OCT imaging, microthermal zones (MZTs) induced by fractional lasers can be noninvasively visualized, and the size of induced MZTs can be quantitatively evaluated. According to the OCT results, the center region of the induced MZT corresponds to weaker backscattered intensity after the AFL exposure as a result of tissue volatilization by photon energy. In contrast, after the NAFL exposure, the skin tissue is damaged and coagulated but not volatilized, which causes the backscattered intensity of the induced MZT enhanced in the OCT image. To further identify the photothermolysis induced by AFLs or NAFLs, the backscattered intensities of MZTs are compared with those of the untreated tissue from the OCT results. The statistical result shows a clear difference in scattering properties of photothermolysis induced by AFLs and NAFLs. Finally, the induced photodamage at various depths can also be quantitatively evaluated, enabling an investigation of the relationship between the photodamage and the depth.

articleTitle: Exa-bit optical communication exploring by 3M scheme
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We present recent challenges and efforts toward a hardware paradigm shift to overcome capacity limitation under current optical communication infrastructure. The latest advances in the three “multi” technologies, i. e. multi-level transmission with ultrahigh spectral efficiency, space division multiplexing in multi-core fibers, and mode division multiplexing with MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output), will be overviewed.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensing with high temperature nano-coated electric arc-induced long-period gratings working at dispersion turning point
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The work presents for a first time electric arc-induced long-period gratings (LPGs) working at dispersion turning point (DTP) in wavelength range about 1550 nm. The DTP has been achieved as a result of reduction in grating period down to about 190 μm. In contradiction to LPGs typically fabricated using UV laser-based method, arc-induced gratings show high thermal stability and a great long-term performance. These advantages allow for coating LPG with thin film deposition methods, which require high temperature. We discuss effect of thin silicon nitride (SiN<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>) overlay deposition with radio frequency plasma enhanced chemical vapour deposition (RF PECVD) method on refractive index sensitivity of the LPGs.

articleTitle: Enhancement of luminescence with resonance waveguide gratings
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: In this study two resonance waveguide gratings with different materials were designed to enhance luminescence effect. The optimization and the fabrication steps of the gratings are described. The theoretical enhancement of the energy densities inside the luminescent material were 1100- and 5200-fold for the two gratings.

articleTitle: Recent developments in gradient index optics
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The University of Rochester and its team members advanced three gradient index (GRIN) material paths towards mass manufacturing and developed the tools needed to integrate these GRIN materials into optical designs.

articleTitle: Optical mode converter using multi-mode interference structure
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate multi-mode interference (MMI) based optical mode converter for spatial multi-mode multiplexing transmission. The implemented device showed mode-conversion of over 35 nm operation band with less than 0.5 dB excess loss, and full C-band operation was confirmed successfully.

articleTitle: Asymmetrical slit Si waveguide TE-TM mode converter
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: An asymmetrical slit waveguide TE-TM mode converter is investigated for integrating with a Si waveguide optical isolator. We fabricated the mode converter of which structure is compatible with a Si Mach-Zehnder interferometer waveguide optical isolator. A TE-TM mode conversion of 89% was measured at a wavelength of 1.55 μm in the device with 8-μm-long slit.

articleTitle: Microoptical systems for consumer's hands
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Microoptical elements like coupling or condenser lens arrays are industrially applied since years for improving the features of optical systems (e.g. optical communication lines, lithography machines). The launch of wafer-level fabricated front cameras in consumer products like cell phones is a breakthrough for microoptical systems. The advances in the explored microoptics technology (polymer-on-glass) are the base for next microoptics based consumer products to market in the coming years.

articleTitle: Single-stripe tunable laser with Chirped Sampled Gratings fabricated by nanoimprint lithography
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Fabrication of diffraction gratings of Chirped Sampled Grating Distributed Reflector (CSG-DR) laser by nanoimprint lithography (NIL) has been demonstrated. The diffraction gratings with highly uniform linewidth and period have been successfully fabricated by the combination of the reverse-tone NIL and precise etching techniques. The fabricated CSG-DR laser using NIL shows sufficiently wide tuning range of 40 nm as we designed.

articleTitle: On realizing bipolar optical access codecs with Walsh-coded liquid crystal modulators
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A realization technique of optical CDMA spectral-coding with bipolar Walsh codes based on SLM codecs was proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The proposal utilizes the phase delay characteristics of SLM to construct our SLM encoder/decoder. The spectral decoder verified the correlations of the Walsh codes and showed that binary data could be recovered by correlation detection. This paper also demonstrated that the system rejects multiple-access interference.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Brillouin scattering properties in plastic optical fibers for wide-range temperature sensing
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We investigate the temperature dependence of Brillouin scattering properties in perfluorinated graded-index (PFGI-) plastic optical fibers (POFs) in a wide temperature range from -170 to 130°C. The temperature dependence of Brillouin frequency shift is found to be nonlinear at > 84°C; while it shows linear dependences even at -170°C. The Stokes power is maximal at ~60 °C and is gradually reduced with decreasing or increasing temperature. Our results indicate that the Brillouin scattering in PFGI-POFs can be exploited to cryogenic-temperature sensing as well as higher-temperature sensing.

articleTitle: Polymer wavelength-selective filter using high-mesa structure directly-coupled double micro-ring resonators
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We fabricated a polymer double micro-ring-resonator wavelength-selective filter, whose ring resonators were directly coupled with MMI each other. The device exhibited the output-power contrasts of 8.5 dB and 10.0 dB for TE and TM mode, respectively.

articleTitle: Single-mode optical waveguide of polysilane irradiated by ultra-violet light
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We have realized optical waveguides using solid polysilane. The refractive index of the polysilane is changed by heating or irradiation for ultra-violet lights of 330 nm wavelength. Optical waveguides are achieved by selective irradiation of the lights to the polysilane. We have designed and fabricated multi-mode optical couplers and single-mode optical waveguides, and experimental results for them were successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Polymer microoptics for VCSEL beam control
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We present recent advances on design and fabrication of SU-8-based tunable microlens for VCSEL (Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Lasers) dynamic focusing. The experimental behaviour of this optical microsystem is found to be in good agreement with a tri-dimensional thermo-mechanical model taking into account SU-8 out-plane properties.

articleTitle: A proposal of novel optical interface to transmit 8K-UHDTV for consumer applications
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Ultra High Definition TV (UHDTV) which is a next-generation video format has been developed in each country. In Japan, test broadcasting of 8Kx4K Ultra High Definition TV (8 K-UHDTV) with 16 times resolution of High Definition TV (HDTV) will be started in 2016. However, there is still no interface which transmits uncompressed 8K-UHDTV between electrical household appliances and electrical equipment. This paper proposes an interface for the transmission apparatus for the household appliances to transmit 120 Gbps 8 K-UHDTV video using GI-POF.

articleTitle: Bit-error-rate performance OF 10-Gb/s silicon Mach-Zehnder modulator module in 100-km optical-fiber transmisson
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: 10-Gb/s Si Mach-Zehnder modulator is packaged in module and its bit-error-rate performance is characterized in 100-km optical-fiber transmission. Fiber coupling is realized using microlenses with 2-dB coupling loss per facet and 32-dB return loss. 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> bit error rate is achieved at 17-dB optical signal-to-noise ratio in 100-km optical-fiber transmission.

articleTitle: Brillouin scattering in erbium-doped optical fibers: Fundamental properties and pumping effect
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: As the first step to develop erbium-doped optical fiber (EDF)-based Brillouin distributed temperature and strain sensing, we measure both the Brillouin gain spectra of EDFs with three different concentrations, and the Brillouin frequency shift dependences on temperature and strain along with their relations to erbium-doping concentration. We also measure the amplification effect of the Brillouin signal in one of the EDFs by 980-nm pumping.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of double phase conjugate mirror for optical inter-satellite communication with large shift tolerance
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We propose an innovative optical inter-satellite communication system with a double phase conjugate mirror. The proposed system improves the acquisition, tracking and background light reduction functions by utilization of phase conjugation. This paper reports on the temporal and spatial characteristics of double phase conjugate mirror to consider large shift tolerance.

articleTitle: Spectroscopy AS a “green” technique for food quality and safety applications
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A selection of spectroscopy-based, fiber optic and micro-optic devices is presented. They have been designed and tested for monitoring the quality and safety of common foodstuffs. The absorption, fluorescence, reflection and Raman spectra, considered as product fingerprints, allowed to detecting quality indicators such as nutraceutic ingredients or indications of the production region, to authenticating products and detecting frauds, as well as spotting out harmful elements.

articleTitle: Silica planar lightwave circuit collimator with UV-cured resin as integrated multilayered lenses
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We propose a silica-based waveguide collimator that introduces UV-cured resin as integrated multilayered lenses. The collimator is applicable for replacing microlens arrays often used in optical systems containing fiber to free-space interconnects. We fabricated and demonstrated beam collimation with the waveguide collimator. The focal distance achieved is around 6 cm.

articleTitle: Modulation response enhancement of transverse-coupled cavity VCSELs for radio over fiber applications
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the high-speed and efficient direct modulation of a novel transverse-coupled-cavity (TCC) VCSEL for radio over fiber applications. An oxide-defined cavity acts as an ultra-compact lateral feedback resonator integrated with a 980nm VCSEL. The modulation amplitude was enhanced by over 25dB in a millimeter-wave band beyond 26 GHz.

articleTitle: Image resolution improvement in digital holographic microscope with image restoration and PSF upscaling
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A image restoration based on deconvolution method is proposed in digital holographic microscopy. To overcome the resolution limit of the optical imaging system, we applied two key concepts: image resizing and PSF (Point Spread Function) upscaling. This method provides detailed and extended frequency components to improve the quality of the image. We demonstrated the digital holographic microscopy system with the proposed image restoration and evaluated its performance. As a result, we confirmed that the proposed method is quite promising for realizing high quality images.

articleTitle: Differential processing using an optical pulse synthesizer and its application to chirp measurement
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Differential processing of optical short pulses was achieved using an optical pulse synthesizer. The chirp of optical short pulses after the fiber transmission was measured with the differential processing.

articleTitle: Fundamental characteristics of 1550nm-band 20-layer-stacked QD-SOA grown on InP(311)B substrate for all-optical logic gate device
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: In this paper, we fabricated the QD-SOA which utilized the highly-stacked quantum dots structure with the strain-compensation technique and MQW-SOA, and compared the measured fundamental characteristics to the one of MQW-SOA.

articleTitle: Speckle noise reduction by focal plane wave-front sensing in high contrast imaging optics
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: For the direct detection of extrasolar planets, a high contrast imaging optics system is required. One of the problems in it is speckle noise due to the wave-front error in the coronagraph optics. We proposed the focal plane wave-front sensing method to reduce the speckle noise and successfully reduced the speckle noise level by 2 order of magnitude.

articleTitle: Recording light fields with microoptical systems
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The most popular device for recording light fields is the plenoptic camera, a system including both a macroscopic lens and a microlens array. We argue that the macroscopic lens can be omitted without compromising light field resolution, drastically simplifying and shrinking the system. We then discuss the limits of miniaturisation and practical fabrication issues.

articleTitle: High-speed and low-voltage operation of compact Bragg reflector waveguide modulator
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: An ultra-compact (<;55μm) and low-voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</sub>=500mV) electro-absorption modulator was demonstrated based on a Bragg reflector waveguide. The miniature device offers 3dB-bandwidth over 13GHz, showing a prospect of ultra-low power-consumption below 100fJ/bit thanks to its low-voltage swing.

articleTitle: 1 × 2 Vertically optical splitter with 10-Gbps transmission rate for chip-level optical interconnects
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A polymer waveguide monolithically integrated with three Si-based 45° reflectors realized on a Si substrate is proposed to form a 1 × 2 vertically optical splitter. A VCSEL chip at the input port and two PD chips at two output ports are flip-chip assembled on the proposed splitter to demonstrate the chip-level optical interconnects. The optical insertion loss of -4 dB with a splitting ratio of 1:1 for the proposed splitter is experimentally obtained. Finally, the reasonable eye patterns with an operating date rate of 10 Gbps at two output ports are also achieved.

articleTitle: Optical inspection and thickness measurement of nanostructures with optical coherence tomography based on single channel acquisition
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Summary form only given. In this study, a phase-sensitive, swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) system is implemented for the optical measurement of nanostructures. A new approach is proposed to reduce the phase errors, resulting from trigger jitter of the swept source and the asynchronization between the A-scan trigger and OCT signal at the data acquisition end, with a narrowband fiber Bragg grating to generate the accurate A-scan trigger. Furthermore, combining the common-path configuration with the proposed approach, the displacement sensitivity can be calculated to be 80 pm when the swept source is operated at 3a kHz. Finally, the conducting glass was scanned with the proposed approach to quantitatively measure the thickness of conducting layer. The results show that the proposed SS-OCT approach can make be a potentially useful tool for noninvasive, real-time inspection of nanostructures.

articleTitle: A wavelength insensitive, non-contact and highly efficient fiber optic connector using up-tapered multimode optical fibers
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: A wavelength independent, non-contact and highly efficient fiber optic connector has been demonstrated. The connector consists of a pair of up-tapered multimode optical fibers. The insertion loss was measured to be 0.9 dB in the wavelength range from 410 to 790 nm. This novel fiber optic connector will find applications in multi-color illumination systems, where frequent plugging and unplugging of the connector are necessary.

articleTitle: Design of polymer waveguide couplers for mode-division-multiplexing applications
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: We design a mode multiplexer/demultiplexer with two cascaded waveguide couplers formed along the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively. The LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> and two orthogonal LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> modes of the waveguide can be spatially separated with a crosstalk lower than 20 dB using a device length shorter than 10 mm. This device could be implemented with the polymer waveguide technology for its ability to realize vertical couplers.

articleTitle: Terahertz transmission through one-nanometer slits
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: Terahertz waves funnel through infinite single slits with a few nanometer gaps, reaching an ultimate limit of electric field enhancement due to high aspect ratio between metal thickness and gap size. Our study provides not only a deep understanding of giant field enhancement through an infinite single slit but also points towards many potential applications in plasmonics, light focusing and strong light matter interaction.

articleTitle: Wafer-level technologies for computational cameras
publicationTitle: Technical Digest of the Eighteenth Microoptics Conference
abstract: The concept of array cameras is a new approach to imaging. It offers unique and exciting possibilities packed in very low z-height. The feature of 3-D imaging will enable new applications in smartphones and will become a must-have. Even very compact array cameras, e.g. in a 2×2 layout, deliver a high resolution video stream and a depth map without any additional hardware. On the hardware side, the lens technology is the key for computational cameras.
